records.author: Boss (Skip Snow)
records.target: Beta Sprint 1 (May 2026). April is quality month — no new components.

three_component_architecture.1: Find Care — find providers, specialties, navigate the system
three_component_architecture.2: Evaluate Care — clinical trials, provider credentials, quality metrics
three_component_architecture.3: Discuss Care — multi-participant AI-assisted healthcare collaboration

records.overview: Multi-participant healthcare collaboration chat. Consumers invite friends, family, and caregivers into a shared AI-assisted session. All participants have access to all healthcare tools. All conversations constrained to healthcare mission.

features.description: Multiple humans in one conversation with AI assistance
User sends invite link to friends, family, caregivers. No account required.
Multiple AI models participate in the same session (Claude, GPT, etc.), each with access to all tools
All participants (human and AI) can trigger provider search, clinical trials, specialty identification, provider detail
Conversations constrained to healthcare navigation. Same safety filter, emergency detection, scope rules.
Exportable transcript for sharing with doctors, care teams
Each participant manages their own consent tier independently
Session creator (host), invited participant (peer). No admin/enterprise roles.
All participants see messages and AI responses live
Sessions survive disconnects, resumable by invite link

Any participant or component can dispatch a research bot to gather information. Shared object across all three components and pipelines. Bot runs autonomously, returns findings to the session. Dispatched by consensus or individual request. All bot work incurs a fee.

features.feature: Licensed Provider Detection and Compliance Disclosure
features.description: If a participant identifies as or is detected as a licensed healthcare provider, the system triggers automatic compliance disclosure: (1) ChatHealthy.ai is not subject to HIPAA, (2) This session does not create a provider-patient relationship, (3) Security standards disclosed (HITRUST/DOD/SOC2). All participants must acknowledge before session continues. Consent re-confirmed.

architectural_implications: Third business component alongside FindCare and EvaluateCareQuality
WebSocket or SSE for real-time multi-user
Session state in MongoDB (participants, messages, consent per user)
Tool access governed by same ToolRouter — no new tools, just shared access
GOV-001 preserved: consumer-only, no payer revenue
DiscussCareFacade as the entry point — same pattern as FindCare and EvaluateCare
records.origin: Boss insight: wanted to invite himself and Perplexity into a conversation. Realized consumers benefit from the same pattern — invite family into a healthcare chat with AI assistance.

revenue_model.name: Choose Your AI
revenue_model.mechanism: AI model providers pay ChatHealthy.ai for access to user sessions
why_they_pay: User attention in healthcare — highest-value decision context
Tool usage generates training signal in healthcare domain
Brand presence at point of care decision
Distribution channel they cannot build themselves
revenue_model.gov_001_compliance: AI vendors are TECHNOLOGY partners, not care-chain entities. No payer, no provider, no pharma revenue. GOV-001 preserved.
revenue_model.pitch: Your model is in the room when a family decides where Mom gets cancer treatment. What's that worth?
revenue_model.user_experience: User selects which AI models participate in their session. Models compete on helpfulness. User pays nothing.
revenue_model.series_a_story: We own the healthcare decision room. AI companies pay to be in it.

moat.regulatory_willingness: AI vendors avoid healthcare regulation like the plague. FDA clinical decision support classification and HIPAA compliance are existential risks for companies valued on growth. They NEED someone else to own the healthcare room.
moat.trust: Consumers chose ChatHealthy.ai for care decisions. Trust takes years to build, seconds to lose.
moat.data: Provider + clinical trials + quality data. Takes years to assemble and curate.
moat.governance: Multi-AI healthcare safety framework. Floor control, consent per participant, emergency detection. Nobody else has this.
moat.network: Every session adds participants and signal. Compound growth.
moat.legal_model: Apple precedent — platform charges both sides. Good lawyers. Not a conflict, a marketplace.

pricing_model.find_care: FREE — 100% free forever. This is the funnel.
pricing_model.evaluate_care: FREE now. Paywall option once trusted brand established. Premium quality metrics, deeper credential analysis, comparative ratings.
pricing_model.discuss_care: Premium token markup on AI usage
pricing_model.principle: All healthcare navigation is free. Users only pay when they choose premium AI models in Discuss Care sessions. The markup on tokens is the ONLY revenue from users.
partnership_path: Stage 1: Sign up for AI vendor partnership/startup programs. Get free credits.
Stage 2: Build relationships with partner team humans. Show real healthcare usage.
Stage 3: Demonstrate value — their model is already in healthcare decision rooms.
Stage 4: Partners underwrite Series A. They've seen the data.
pricing_model.gov_001_note: Token revenue is from technology consumption, not care-chain entities. GOV-001 preserved.

patent_concept.claim: Method for synthesizing healthcare provider quality signals using large language models to produce consumer-comprehensible provider assessments
patent_concept.innovation: All signals are public. LLMs exist. The method of combining them for consumer healthcare navigation is novel.
next_steps: Provisional patent draft in Discuss Care beta session (Boss + Claude + GPT + patent lawyer)
patent_concept.first_use_case_for_discuss_care: Drafting the provisional patent IS the beta test of the product.

research_bot.name: Shared Research Bot
research_bot.scope: Cross-component shared object — not owned by any single component
capabilities: Autonomous research tasks dispatched from any component
Clinical trial matching and eligibility analysis
Returns structured findings to requesting session or pipeline
research_bot.billing: All bot research incurs token fees — premium revenue stream
research_bot.architectural_note: Shared service, not inside any facade. Accessible via all three facades and pipeline orchestrator.

governance_rules.description: Doctors, providers, and licensed clinicians are NEVER participants in a Discuss Care session. The session transcript is shared WITH the doctor after. The doctor is never IN the room.
governance_rules.rationale: Provider presence creates clinical decision support risk (FDA), malpractice exposure, and transforms the platform from consumer navigation to clinical tool. This boundary is permanent.

governance_rules.description: ChatHealthy.ai is NOT a HIPAA covered entity and is NOT subject to HIPAA regulations. We are a consumer navigation platform, not a healthcare provider or business associate. However, we voluntarily adopt enterprise-grade security standards to protect user data.
security_standards: DOD-level security audit standard (FedRAMP or equivalent)
governance_rules.disclosure_requirement: Every session and every document must disclose: (1) We are not subject to HIPAA. (2) We voluntarily maintain audited security at enterprise healthcare standards. (3) Even if a participant happens to be a licensed provider, the platform remains a consumer tool and does not create a provider-patient relationship.
governance_rules.rationale: Neutrality requires transparency. We earn trust by choosing to be secure, not by being compelled. This avoids HIPAA regulatory burden while exceeding the security expectations of healthcare buyers.

marketing_positioning.headline: We are not required to protect your data. We choose to. And we do it better than the ones who are required to.
marketing_positioning.context: Healthcare organizations suffer constant data breaches DESPITE being under HIPAA. HIPAA is a compliance checkbox, not a security guarantee. ChatHealthy.ai voluntarily adopts HITRUST/DOD-level security because our business depends on consumer trust, not regulatory compulsion.
marketing_use: Landing page trust badge: "Voluntarily HITRUST certified — exceeding HIPAA standards"
Investor pitch: security by choice signals product-market fit and consumer-first values
Enterprise sales: healthcare buyers trust voluntary security over mandatory compliance
Competitive differentiation: incumbents are breached monthly under HIPAA. We choose higher standards.
Press/PR: "The healthcare platform that protects your data better than your hospital does"
marketing_positioning.why_it_works: Consumers instinctively trust companies that choose to do the right thing over companies forced to. Voluntary security is a brand asset, not a cost center.

security_certifications_path.what: Healthcare-specific security framework. Gold standard for health tech. Maps to HIPAA, NIST, ISO 27001.
security_certifications_path.why: Healthcare buyers require it. Proves we exceed HIPAA without being subject to it.

security_certifications_path.what: Independent audit of security controls over 6-12 months. Trust Services Criteria.
security_certifications_path.why: Enterprise table stakes. Proves operational security, not just policy.

security_certifications_path.what: DOD standard for protecting Controlled Unclassified Information. 110 security controls.
security_certifications_path.why: Direct path to FedRAMP. If VA or DOD wants ChatHealthy, we are ready.
Transparency. We publish what hospitals hide.

records.vision: ChatHealthy.ai provides the data, tools, and an AI-enlightened space to empower regular people to prevail over the broken healthcare system. Whatever a person's circumstances might be, they deserve the best possible care, at the best value. ChatHealthy.ai gives them the platform to get it. By presenting and evaluating care options but never giving medical advice, the platform allows families, individuals, and friends to collaborate with the most powerful AI models in order to choose the best provider they can have.
records.mission: Help people make better healthcare decisions together.

funding_model.key_insight: AI vendors are CAPITAL, not income. They fund the ramp-up. Consumer token markup is the revenue.
capital_sources: Anthropic — partnership program, then Series A participation
OpenAI — partnership program, then Series A participation
Google — partnership program, then Series A participation
NVIDIA — infrastructure partnership, GPU credits, investment arm
funding_model.distinction: Vendor access fees fund growth (capital). Consumer token markup funds operations (revenue). Do not confuse the two in the pitch.
funding_model.pitch_framing: We buy tokens at your rate. We resell at a premium. You fund our growth so your model is in the healthcare decision room. Both sides win.

records.report: FindCare Backend Portability Refactoring — Design Report

problem_statement.summary: The FindCare backend is a 1,323-line monolithic main.py. All business logic, FastAPI setup, prompt construction, tool dispatch, safety checks, provider search, clinical trials, lead capture, notifications, and static file serving live in one file. Porting to a different host (e.g., Azure App Service) requires touching the monolith.
problem_statement.boss_directive: Porting to Azure should not be major work. Portability must be a design property, not an afterthought.
problem_statement.trigger: Delaware Division of Professional Regulation board search URL (https://dpr.delaware.gov/boardsearch/) returns 404 — exposed the need for URL validation AND highlighted how tightly coupled the app is to its hosting environment.

design.principle: Separate what changes per host from what never changes. All business logic is host-agnostic. Only HostConfig and the entry point know where the app is running.

modules.responsibility: Thin entry point. Creates HostConfig from environment, wires URLGuardian, PromptFactory, and FindCareApp together, hands them to GUIHelper, starts the server.
All host-specific configuration in one place. Factory method from_env() reads environment variables with sensible defaults.

modules.constructor: FindCareApp(host_config: HostConfig, prompt_factory: PromptFactory, url_guardian: URLGuardian)
modules.responsibility: ALL business logic. Safety system, provider search, clinical trials, lead capture, chat conversation loop, tool dispatch, notifications, debug logging. Creates its own MongoDB connection and Anthropic/OpenAI clients internally.

Creates the FastAPI app instance. Configures CORS. Registers endpoints (/health, /welcome, /chat). Mounts static files if host_config.mount_static_files is true. Defines Pydantic request/response models.
Loads context documents (PDFs, text files) at init. Constructs the system prompt. Holds the Anthropic tool schema list. Maintains a tool registry (name -> callable) for dispatch.

tool_registry.what: dict[str, Callable] mapping tool names to function references
tool_registry.why: Replaces globals().get(name) — explicit registration, no magic lookup
tool_registry.dispatch: FindCareApp._handle_tool_calls does: fn = self.prompt_factory.get_tool(name); result = fn(**args)

modules.responsibility: Validates URLs in tool results and LLM text responses. Removes broken links, follows redirects, caches results.

methods.check_url(url): Returns (is_valid, redirect_url). HEAD request with GET fallback.
methods.guard_tool_result(result): Validates URLs in a tool result dict. Removes broken links from the 'links' key.
methods.guard_text(text): Validates markdown links and bare URLs in text. Defangs broken links (keeps text, removes href).

features: HEAD request with GET fallback on HTTP 405
Redirect following — updates URL if server redirects
Trusted domain whitelist — Healthgrades, Zocdoc skip validation (bot protection blocks server-side requests)
In-memory TTL cache — avoids repeated HEAD requests within cache window
Concurrent validation — ThreadPoolExecutor for batch URL checks

decisions.gpt_proposed: 11 modules — separate files for DatabaseHelpers, NotificationService, ProviderTools, ClinicalTrialsSearch, ExternalProviderLookup, ContextLoader, ToolDefinitions, etc.
decisions.claude_decided: 5 modules + HostConfig dataclass. Single-function concerns stay as private methods inside FindCareApp.
decisions.rationale: Over-fragmentation adds import complexity for no testability gain. ClinicalTrialsSearch is one function. NotificationService is one function. These don't justify their own files.
decisions.risk_of_this_decision: findcare_app.py is ~800 lines — still large. Acceptable because it's cohesive (all business logic) and can be further split in a future sprint if needed.

decisions.topic: Dependency injection for MongoDB and notifications
decisions.gpt_proposed: Inject DatabaseManager and NotificationService into FindCareApp constructor for testability.
decisions.claude_decided: FindCareApp creates its own MongoDB connection and SparkPost notifier internally. NOT injected.
decisions.rationale: Boss rule: e2e tests use real systems (MongoDB, Anthropic, SparkPost) — no mocks. DI for testability is pointless when you don't mock. Injecting adds constructor complexity for zero practical benefit.
decisions.risk_of_this_decision: Harder to unit test FindCareApp in isolation. Mitigated by the fact that this project's testing strategy is e2e with real systems.

decisions.gpt_proposed: _handle_tool_calls lives in PromptFactory alongside tool schemas.
decisions.claude_decided: Tool dispatch stays in FindCareApp. PromptFactory holds only the registry (name -> callable map) and tool schemas.
decisions.rationale: Tool functions (find_providers, record_user_details, etc.) live in FindCareApp and need access to FindCareApp state (DB connection, chat history, IP locks). Dispatch must be in the same class. The registry pattern decouples schema definition from implementation.
decisions.risk_of_this_decision: FindCareApp has a dependency on PromptFactory for the registry. Acceptable — they're always used together.

decisions.gpt_proposed: Validate URLs in the final LLM text response only.
decisions.claude_decided: Dual-mode: validate both tool results (guard_tool_result) and LLM text (guard_text).
decisions.rationale: Tool-constructed URLs are the higher-priority fix — we build them deterministically (e.g., Delaware board search). If we know the URL template is broken, we should catch it before the LLM even sees it. Text validation catches anything the LLM generates or hallucinates.
decisions.risk_of_this_decision: Two validation points means two places to maintain. Acceptable — both use the same URLGuardian instance and cache.

decisions.claude_decided: Healthgrades and Zocdoc are whitelisted — their search URLs skip validation.
decisions.rationale: Both sites aggressively block server-side requests (bot protection). Our constructed search URLs (e.g., healthgrades.com/search?what=smith) are valid browser URLs but return 403/blocking pages to HEAD/GET from a server. Whitelisting prevents false negatives.
decisions.risk_of_this_decision: If Healthgrades or Zocdoc change their URL patterns, broken links would not be caught. Mitigated by the fact that we construct these URLs ourselves with known patterns.

decisions.claude_decided: FindCareApp owns a single Anthropic client instance, created in __init__.
decisions.rationale: Currently the Anthropic client is created fresh in _chat_inner and _safety_check on every call. A single shared instance avoids repeated initialization and is the standard pattern for API clients.
decisions.risk_of_this_decision: None — Anthropic SDK client is thread-safe.

decisions.topic: Sprint timing — defer refactoring to Sprint 2
decisions.boss_decided: Do not refactor before the Tuesday 2026-03-31 release. Ship URLGuardian now, refactoring in Sprint 2.
decisions.rationale: App is release-ready. Refactoring 1,323 lines of working code 3 days before deadline is risk with no user-facing payoff. Quality over velocity.
decisions.risk_of_this_decision: main.py stays monolithic through Sprint 1 release. Acceptable — it works, and URLGuardian is the only new capability needed now.

risks.risk: Refactoring may introduce subtle bugs in tool dispatch or chat conversation loop
risks.impact: High — broken chat is a showstopper
risks.mitigation: Each migration step produces a working app. Full e2e test after each step. Stop at any step if tests fail.

risks.risk: URL validation adds latency to chat responses
risks.impact: Medium — user waits longer for responses
risks.mitigation: Concurrent HEAD requests (ThreadPoolExecutor). TTL cache avoids repeated checks. Trusted domain whitelist skips bot-protected sites. Timeout of 5 seconds per URL.

risks.risk: Large PR — 1,300 lines moved across 5 files
risks.impact: Medium — hard to review, merge conflicts with any parallel work
risks.mitigation: Incremental migration steps. Each step is a separate commit. Can stop after any step with a working app.

risks.risk: Trusted domain whitelist becomes stale — Healthgrades/Zocdoc change URL patterns
risks.impact: Low — worst case is a working but outdated search URL
risks.mitigation: We construct these URLs ourselves. If patterns change, update the URL construction in lookup_provider_external.

risks.risk: findcare_app.py at ~800 lines is still large
risks.impact: Low — it's cohesive (all business logic), just long
risks.mitigation: Can further split in a future sprint if needed. Provider tools and safety system are natural extraction candidates.

records.copyright: Copyright 2026 Skip Snow. All rights reserved.
records.executive_summary: Modular monolith refactor of FindCare backend from a 1,712-line main.py monolith to a facade-oriented domain architecture. Two business domains (FindCare, EvaluateCareQuality) with explicit service classes per UAT feature. HuggingFace reduced to entrypoint + adapter only. Strangler Fig migration in 7 phases, zero downtime, deployable at every phase. Pydantic-enforced tool boundaries. Full Perplexity audit response covering all 18 findings.

layers: Domain Layer (Business Services per UAT feature)
Infrastructure Layer (MongoDB, External APIs, Embeddings, Config)
top_level_architecture.dependency_direction: Host -> Application -> Domain -> Infrastructure (no upward imports)

NLP taxonomy mapping, specialty code lookup

Full two-tier HIPAA consent workflow — see Section 4.1 Consent Flow Detail
Static content loading for about intents
Dual-mode URL validation (tool results + LLM text)

consent_flow.title: Consent Framework — Full Workflow Design
consent_flow.description: HIPAA-aligned two-tier consent framework controlling what user data is stored and how. Consent is a full-time workflow — not a flag. It governs the entire data lifecycle of a user session.
consent_flow.trigger: Every 5th user message, system prompt instructs Claude to ask: 'Would you like someone from ChatHealthy.AI to follow up with you personally?'

tiers.name: Verbatim Consent
tiers.prompt: May we save a verbatim transcript of this conversation with your contact details?

if_yes.stored: Full chat_history (PII intact), email, name, notes, reason_for_contact
if_yes.evidence: Consent exchange itself is included in the stored transcript

tiers.name: De-Identified Summary Consent
tiers.prompt: May we save a de-identified summary of this conversation instead?

if_yes.stored: LLM-generated summary passed through deIdentify() — no PII, no chat_history
if_yes.process: Claude summarizes -> deIdentify() scrubs PII -> stored in notes field

if_no.stored: Contact fields only (email, name). No history, no summary.

data_streams.treatment: Always de-identified before storage. No PII. No consent needed.
Two-tier consent governs what is stored. User chooses verbatim or summary.

integration_points: ChatOrchestrator: triggers consent prompt every 5th message
LeadService: delegates to ConsentService for data handling
System Prompt: RULE 7 defines the consent UX flow
deIdentify(): shared utility used by ConsentService and UnknownQuestionService
regulatory_notes: Consent exchange itself must be preserved as evidence (included in verbatim transcript)
De-identification must be applied BEFORE storage, not after
Emergency records (BTC-003) must NEVER be deleted regardless of consent state
Test data tagged with testdata=true for filtering

growth_trajectory.note: This service will GROW, not diminish. Consent is a first-class, expanding concern.
planned_additions: Granular consent: per-data-type consent (contact info separate from conversation history)
Consent revocation: user can withdraw consent after the fact — must retroactively de-identify or delete
Consent audit trail: immutable log of every consent grant, revocation, and data action
HIPAA minimum necessary: only collect what is needed for the stated purpose
Consent expiration: time-limited consent with re-confirmation workflow
Enterprise consent: when healthcare orgs use the platform, their compliance policies override defaults
Consent portability: export consent records for regulatory audit (state AG, HHS OCR)
Multi-jurisdiction: state-specific consent rules (e.g., California CCPA, NY SHIELD, HIPAA federal)
growth_trajectory.architectural_implication: ConsentService must be its own bounded context with dedicated tools, dedicated pydantic models, dedicated tests, and dedicated audit logging. It is NOT a helper inside LeadService.

pydantic_models: ConsentAuditEntry: session_id, action, tier, timestamp, evidence_hash

architectural_decisions.decision: Facade-oriented domains over flat service layer
architectural_decisions.rationale: Two business domains (FindCare, EvaluateCareQuality) each get a facade. Facades are the ONLY entry point from ToolRouter to domain services. Prevents cross-domain coupling.
Claude sends JSON tool arguments. Pydantic validates at the ToolRouter before reaching domain services. Catches schema mismatches early.

architectural_decisions.decision: System prompt stays in ChatOrchestrator (not PromptBuilder)
architectural_decisions.rationale: Per Boss decision. Prompt references tool names only (not class names). ToolRouter is source of truth for available tools.

architectural_decisions.decision: Provider Detail belongs to EvaluateCareQuality (not FindCare)
architectural_decisions.rationale: Provider detail is a quality evaluation concern (NPI lookup, board certifications, ratings). Finding a provider and evaluating their quality are distinct business actions.

architectural_decisions.decision: Frontend remains thin — no domain duplication
architectural_decisions.rationale: All domain logic stays server-side. Frontend is presentation-only: ChatWindow, MessageBubble, EmergencyBanner. No backend domain structure mirrored.
7 phases, each deployable. Old functions remain callable until replaced. Zero downtime throughout migration.

current_state.problem: Monolithic — all business logic, FastAPI setup, prompt construction, tool dispatch, safety, providers, clinical trials, lead capture, notifications, and static file serving in a single file.
current_state.sprint_1_mitigation: URLGuardian class extracted as standalone module (url_guardian.py) — validates URLs in tool results and LLM text responses. Integrated into main.py with 3 lines of code.

main.py.responsibility: Thin entry point — creates HostConfig, wires dependencies, starts server
pseudocode: # Register tools from both FindCareApp and PromptFactory

host_config.py.factory: HostConfig.from_env() reads all values from environment variables with sensible defaults

findcare_app.py.responsibility: ALL business logic — safety, providers, clinical trials, lead capture, chat loop, tool dispatch
findcare_app.py.constructor: FindCareApp(host_config: HostConfig, prompt_factory: PromptFactory, url_guardian: URLGuardian)
findcare_app.py.internal_dependencies: Creates its own MongoDB connection (ChatHealthyMongoUtilities), Anthropic client, OpenAI client, SparkPost notifier. These are NOT injected — they are implementation details.

gui_helper.py.responsibility: FastAPI app creation, CORS, endpoints, static file mount
gui_helper.py.delegates: All business logic calls go to FindCareApp

prompt_factory.py.responsibility: System prompt construction, tool schemas, tool registry, context loading

tool_registry.registry: dict[str, Callable] — tool name to function reference
tool_registry.register_tool(name, fn): Adds a tool to the registry
tool_registry.get_tool(name): Returns the callable for a tool name
tool_registry.note: FindCareApp populates the registry at init time. Replaces globals().get(name) pattern.

dual_mode.guard_tool_result(result): Validates URLs in tool result dicts (e.g. lookup_provider_external). Removes broken links.
dual_mode.guard_text(text): Validates URLs in markdown text. Defangs broken links (keeps text, removes href).

features: HEAD request with GET fallback on 405
Redirect following — updates URL if redirected
Trusted domain whitelist (Healthgrades, Zocdoc) — skip validation for bot-protected search sites
In-memory TTL cache — avoids repeated requests

claude_overrides.resolution: Consolidated to 5+1 (HostConfig). Small files like NotificationService, ClinicalTrialsSearch, ExternalProviderLookup are private methods inside FindCareApp, not separate modules.
claude_overrides.reason: Over-fragmentation adds import complexity for no testability gain. These are single-function concerns.

claude_overrides.issue: GPT wanted DatabaseManager and NotificationService injected into FindCareApp
claude_overrides.resolution: FindCareApp creates its own MongoDB and notification internals
claude_overrides.reason: Boss rule: e2e tests use real systems, no mocks. DI for testability is pointless when you don't mock.

claude_overrides.resolution: Tool dispatch stays in FindCareApp. PromptFactory holds the registry (name->callable map).
claude_overrides.reason: Tool functions live in FindCareApp. Dispatch needs access to FindCareApp state (chat history, DB). Registry pattern decouples schema from implementation.

claude_overrides.issue: GPT proposed URL validation on text only
claude_overrides.resolution: Dual-mode: guard_tool_result (for constructed URLs) + guard_text (for LLM-generated markdown)
claude_overrides.reason: Tool-constructed URLs (like the broken Delaware board search) are the higher-priority fix. Text validation catches LLM hallucinated URLs.
